findings.claim: Snapshot admission fails for an authorized empty snapshot because it tries to build a snapshot_id using a zero synthetic barrier and then still emits SnapshotComplete, but the accepted/start checkpoint semantics expose a post-snapshot checkpoint that can skip unseen filtered history.
findings.evidence: In `snapshot_frames`, `barrier` is derived only from authorized deliveries via `disclosed_barrier`; when there are no authorized rows it becomes `commit_lsn: 0` (snapshot.rs lines 9-21), while the `SnapshotComplete` checkpoint is issued from the durable projection cursor (`cursor.as_ref().map(|value| value.broker_offset)`) at lines 390-394. This advances the client past filtered/out-of-scope rows without any visible row or barrier position, conflicting with acceptance B's reconnect/resume requirement and the evidence claim that filtered rows advance only inside an opaque checkpoint without causing skipped protected delivery.
findings.suggested_fix: For empty/fully-filtered snapshots, either make the completion checkpoint the same pre-snapshot checkpoint as `Accepted.start_checkpoint`, or include an explicit resnapshot/filtered-progress contract and prove resume cannot skip newly authorized rows after authorization changes.
